headline: Day-Use Preservation and Gateway Lodging
reservation: Barataria Preserve is a day-use area and does not offer overnight accommodations inside the park. Nearby communities like Lafitte and Marrero provide lodging; check with private providers for availability as the preserve itself does not manage these bookings.

days.title: Swamp Boardwalks and Ancient Middens

stops.name: Bayou Coquille Trail
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalk through cypress-tupelo swamp to see archaeological shell middens left by indigenous cultures.

stops.name: Marsh Overlook
stops.detail: Continue to the end of the boardwalk for expansive views of the freshwater marsh ecosystem.

days.driving: Allow 30-45 minutes from New Orleans; traffic on the West Bank can vary.
days.note: Carry water and insect repellent even on these shorter, flat boardwalk sections.

days.title: Delta Forests and Wildlife

stops.name: Palmetto Trail
stops.detail: Walk through a dense forest of dwarf palmettos that offer a glimpse into the region's prehistoric landscape.

stops.name: Preserve Visitor Center
stops.detail: View the educational exhibits and film detailing how the Mississippi River delta was formed.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes between different preserve trailhead parking lots.
days.note: The Visitor Center has specific operating hours; check the NPS site for current schedules.

days.title: Bayou Waterways

stops.name: Twin Canals
stops.detail: Observe alligators and turtles sunning along the banks of these historic waterways from the shoreline.

stops.name: Lafitte Public Boat Launch
stops.detail: Access the water via local launches for a perspective of the marsh that boardwalks cannot provide.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes to travel from the main preserve entrance to the town of Lafitte.
days.note: Paddling requires monitoring wind conditions, which can make open marsh navigation difficult.

intel.title: Preserve Trailhead Lots
intel.text: Small parking lots are located at the Bayou Coquille and Palmetto trailheads. These can fill during spring weekends, so arriving early is suggested.

intel.title: Wetland Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally available near the Visitor Center but can drop off deep in the swamp. Print or save trail maps before arriving at the preserve.

intel.title: West Bank Services
intel.text: The preserve is in a rural area; the nearest fuel and convenience stores are in Marrero or Lafitte. Ensure you have supplies before entering the park boundaries.

intel.title: Mosquito and Heat Peaks
intel.text: Humidity and insect activity are highest from June through September. Mornings are generally more comfortable for walking the exposed marsh trails.

intel.title: Boardwalk Conditions
intel.text: Heavy rain or flooding can occasionally close sections of the boardwalks. Check the official NPS 'Alerts' page for daily trail status updates.

plan.arrival: Fly into MSY airport and pick up a rental car; stop in Marrero for essentials before the final 15-mile drive to the preserve entrance.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are perfectly suitable for the paved roads leading to the preserve; no off-road capability is required.
plan.goldenHour: The Marsh Overlook provides a wide horizon for sunset, though the park gates have specific closing times to respect.
